speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with painful urination, and a history of a similar episode in your left ankle. To understand the connection between these symptoms, have you noticed any rash, fever, or eye irritation recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome).

The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (knee and history of ankle), urethritis (painful urination), and recent sexual activity with inconsistent condom use is highly suggestive of this condition. Given the patient's age and symptoms, further evaluation with inflammatory markers and joint aspiration is warranted. REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP, Urinalysis.
